item.text: I’m reviewing the remaining connections from memory, with attention to whether each adds a distinct scene, continuation, root use, or interpretation. I’ll save only new proposals to `followup.tsv`.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > '/Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec8/sol/followup.tsv' <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Gen.37.31	goat blood prepared as evidence	The commentary's Jacob receives a bloodied object with a false story; Genesis says the brothers slaughter a goat and dip Joseph's tunic in its blood before sending it, identifying the evidence as manufactured.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.4.8	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary makes belief follow examination of what is perceived; God says that if the people do not believe or heed the first sign, they may believe the second, treating signs as successive grounds for assent.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.4.31	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary moves from transmitted words and seen evidence to faith; Israel hears that the Lord has visited them, sees Moses' signs, believes, and bows in response.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.18.22	failed prediction tests a claim	The commentary demands investigation before confirming a report; Deuteronomy says a prophet's word that fails to happen was not spoken by the Lord, giving hearers a public test.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.28.9	outcome identifies true messenger	The commentary's truth must match the thing reported; Jeremiah says a prophet announcing peace is known as truly sent when the predicted word comes to pass.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.23.1	false report must not be carried	The commentary ends with recommending verified truth to others; Israel is forbidden to spread a false report or aid a malicious witness, making transmission itself an ethical act.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.18.13	answer before hearing	The commentary begins with hearing before judgment; Proverbs calls replying before one hears a matter folly and shame, showing the cost of skipping examination.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.12.11	ear tests words	The commentary treats hearing as the start of active verification; Job asks whether the ear tests words as the palate tastes food, making sensory discrimination a model for judging speech.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.2	search out a matter	The commentary's hakaktu'l-emr means probing a matter until certain; Proverbs calls searching out a concealed matter the glory of kings, giving inquiry a positive role.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.53.1	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary defines belief as crediting a communicated truth; Isaiah asks who has believed the speakers' report and to whom the Lord's arm has been revealed, pairing received testimony with disclosure.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Num.14.11	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary lets observed signs support belief; God asks how long Israel will refuse to believe him despite all the signs performed among them, showing sight need not secure assent.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.78.32	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary can read loss as blindness despite evidence; the psalm says Israel still sinned and did not believe God's wonders after witnessing them.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.119.66	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary links mental discernment and assent; the psalmist asks to be taught judgment and knowledge because he has believed God's commandments.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Neh.8.6	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary's assent to truth becomes submission; the assembly answers Amen twice to Ezra's blessing, lifts its hands, and bows, using the corresponding root as communal affirmation.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.73.16	ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence	The commentary explicitly calls for exerting the mind and the far-looking eye; the psalmist says trying to understand the wicked's prosperity was toil in his eyes.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.73.17	sanctuary resolves inquiry	The commentary's mental labor leads toward seeing what is true; after struggling to understand, the psalmist enters God's sanctuary and discerns the prosperous wicked's end.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Eccl.8.17	ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence	The commentary's inquiry culminates in certainty; Qoheleth says a human may toil to search God's work and still fail to find it, setting a concrete limit on investigative labor.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.10.14	ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence	The commentary joins noticing hardship with an orphan's need for care; the psalm says God sees trouble and vexation, takes it in hand, and helps the fatherless, with the Hebrew toil root naming what is seen.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.119.155	ح ق ق / חקק; table sound correspondence	The commentary connects loss and salvation with acting on what is right; the psalm says salvation is far from the wicked because they do not seek God's statutes, using the Hebrew root for prescribed order.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.3.11	seen knowledge testified	The commentary takes observed truth into shared testimony; Jesus says he and his companions speak what they know and testify to what they have seen, while hearers reject their witness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.6.36	seeing without believing	The commentary's sight can lead to faith but does not guarantee it; Jesus tells his hearers that they have seen him and yet do not believe.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.6.40	seeing and believing joined	The commentary describes a movement from vision to assent; Jesus joins looking on the Son and believing in him to the promise of eternal life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.8.46	truth told but disbelieved	The commentary's hak is truth that can be confirmed and conveyed; Jesus asks why his hearers do not believe him if he tells the truth.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.12.37	signs seen yet disbelieved	The commentary warns that human sight can fail to become faith; despite many signs done before the people, John says they did not believe Jesus.
strong	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:John.12.38	Isaiah's unbelieved report reread	The commentary connects seeing, a reported truth, and failed belief; John applies Isaiah 53:1's question about the unbelieved report to Jesus' rejected signs, making the prophetic report a reading of that scene.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.18.37	hearers of truth hear witness	The commentary ends with truth conveyed after confirmation; Jesus says he came to testify to the truth and that everyone belonging to truth hears his voice.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.10.17	faith comes through hearing	The commentary begins with auditory perception before assent; Paul says faith comes from hearing the message of Christ, making the received word a route to belief.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.1.2	eyewitnesses transmit	The commentary moves from firsthand perception to handing on truth; Luke names eyewitnesses and ministers of the word as those who delivered the account later investigated by him.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.24.11	report initially disbelieved	The commentary treats a report as something hearers may refuse pending confirmation; the apostles regard the women's resurrection account as nonsense and do not believe them.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.24.39	see and touch to verify	The commentary seeks certainty beyond a received report; the risen Jesus invites the disciples to look at his hands and feet and touch him to verify that he has a body.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.28.17	vision with lingering doubt	The commentary's seeing does not automatically yield assurance; disciples see the risen Jesus and worship him, yet some doubt.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.12.15	report of Peter rejected	The commentary's hearers must judge a report before accepting it; the praying group tells Rhoda she is out of her mind when she reports that Peter is at the door.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.12.16	sight confirms disputed report	The commentary moves from relayed news to seeing for oneself; when Peter keeps knocking, the group opens the door, sees him, and is astonished.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.26.16	vision appoints a witness	The commentary's observer must pass on what was seen; Paul says the risen Jesus appeared to appoint him a witness to what he had seen and what would yet be shown.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.26.18	eyes opened toward faith	The commentary permits loss as blindness and belief as sight; Paul's commission is to open eyes and turn people from darkness to light so they receive a share among those sanctified by faith.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.2.14	observed conduct tested by truth	The commentary joins seeing, truth, and deeds; Paul says he saw that Peter and others were not walking straight according to the gospel's truth and challenged Peter publicly.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.2.12	unbelief in truth and unrighteousness	The commentary's exception joins belief, truth, and righteous conduct against loss; Paul speaks of judgment on those who did not believe truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.1.24	sight forgotten without action	The commentary makes visual recognition part of a path to deeds; James' mirror viewer goes away and immediately forgets what he saw, explaining why the hearer who does not act fails.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:3John.1.3	testimony confirmed by a life	The commentary links transmitted truth and right deeds; brothers testify to Gaius's truth just as he walks in truth, letting conduct corroborate their report.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.3.17	false assurance is blindness	The commentary reads human loss as failure to see oneself rightly; the Laodicean speaker claims wealth and needlessness without knowing he is wretched, poor, and blind.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.3.18	eye salve to see	The commentary makes seeing a corrective to mistaken assurance; the risen Christ counsels Laodicea to obtain salve for its eyes so it may see its condition.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.45.28	Jacob seeks his own sight	The commentary's Jacob moves from a doubtful report toward confirmation; after the wagons revive him, he says Joseph is alive and resolves to go see him before he dies.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Kgs.22.28	prophetic claim exposed to outcome	The commentary demands a true report be confirmable; Micaiah publicly says that if Ahab returns safely, the Lord did not speak by him, making fulfillment a test of his message.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Kgs.3.26	mother revealed by response	The commentary's inquiry tests a claim rather than taking words alone; Solomon's threat to divide the child elicits the real mother's plea to preserve its life.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:1Kgs.3.27	judgment after the test	The commentary moves from evidence to assured judgment; Solomon gives the living child to the woman whose plea disclosed her maternal care.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.2.4	search as for silver	The commentary describes strenuous mental inquiry; Proverbs makes seeking wisdom like searching for hidden treasure, giving effort a concrete image.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.2.5	search yields understanding	The commentary's mental work leads to knowing what is true; Proverbs says the search for wisdom results in understanding fear of the Lord and finding knowledge of God.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Ps.9.21	ء ن س / אנש; table BDB-cited cognate	The commentary's insan is a perceiver who must know his condition; the psalm asks that nations learn they are enosh, making recognition of mortality itself the point.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Job.15.14	ء ن س / אנש; table BDB-cited cognate	The commentary holds human loss beside righteous action; Eliphaz asks what frail enosh is that he could be pure or born of woman and righteous, pressing the gap between human condition and upright deeds.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.28.16	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary pairs belief with patience; Isaiah says the one trusting the tested cornerstone will not act in haste, linking assent with steadiness.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Exod.17.12	ء م ن / אמנ; table sound correspondence	The commentary's faith and patience accompany Moses; his hands remain steady during the battle, illustrating the Hebrew root's physical firmness rather than verbal assent.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Job.4.8	ع م ل / עמל; table sound correspondence	The commentary distinguishes righteous work from loss; Job's friend says those who sow trouble reap it, using the toil root for harmful effort with a ruinous result.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.24.5	ح ق ق / חקק; table sound correspondence	The commentary joins truth and right conduct against loss; Isaiah says inhabitants pollute the earth by transgressing laws and violating an ordinance, showing the Hebrew root in a communal failure to keep prescribed order.
medium	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Job.38.33	ح ق ق / חקק; table sound correspondence	The commentary's observer strives for certainty; God asks Job whether he knows the ordinances of heaven, placing the corresponding root in a question about the limits of human knowledge.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.29.16	unfamiliar claim searched out	The commentary's orphan example requires careful guardianship and judgment; Job says he was a father to the needy and investigated a cause he did not know, joining care with inquiry.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.9.7	companions hear but do not see	The commentary distinguishes hearing from seeing in a journey encounter; Saul's companions hear a voice yet see no person, showing that the same event gives witnesses different evidence.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.18.26	received teaching corrected	The commentary's truth is conveyed between people after examination; Priscilla and Aquila hear Apollos and explain God's way to him more accurately.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.15	truth spoken for shared growth	The commentary's believers recommend truth to one another; Ephesians calls for speaking truth in love so the body grows into Christ.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.1.16	eyewitnesses against invented tale	The commentary asks whether a transmitted account rests on perception; Peter rejects clever myths and appeals to eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.13.13	seeing and hearing without understanding	The commentary reads loss as failure to perceive despite eyes and ears; Jesus explains parables by saying people see without seeing and hear without understanding.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Avot 3:9	deeds exceed wisdom	The commentary places mental work beside righteous deeds; this saying holds that wisdom endures when a person's deeds exceed it, making practice a test of learned insight.
EOF"
